key_insight: WC–Co–Cr coating properties depend on powder morphology and spray method: detonation spraying yields higher hardness, while HVOF produces a dense, uniform coating with low friction.
engineering_relevance: Matching feedstock and spray process to service demands can improve the wear resistance and durability of machine parts under high loads and intensive friction.
method: Compare WC–Co–Cr coatings deposited by detonation spraying and HVOF.
Examine powder morphology and coating microstructure using SEM and EDS.
Evaluate coating microhardness and tribological behavior.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports average microhardness of 1449 HV for detonation-sprayed coatings and a friction coefficient of Kt = 0.143 for HVOF coatings.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify test conditions, variability, or quantitative wear rates, limiting direct translation to service performance.
paper_title: INVESTIGATION OF THE FORMATION OF STRUCTURE AND WEAR-RESISTANT PROPERTIES OF WC–CO–CR COATINGS PRODUCED BY HVOF AND DETONATION SPRAYING
